name: content-tier-diagnostic
title: Content Tier Diagnostic
desc: Classifies a piece of writing into one of three tiers—commodity, personality, or original—before publishing. Triggers when a user asks "is this good content," "why does my writing sound like AI," requests an audit of a draft, or wants to know if content is AI slop. Explains why "I" vs "you" framing shifts a piece between tiers and helps decide whether a draft needs rework or is ready to ship.

name: build-digital-brain-content-system
title: Build a Digital Brain / Personal Language Model
desc: Guides building a repeatable "digital brain" system for content creation where AI reuses approved language and crystallized points of view instead of regenerating generic text each time. Trigger on requests like "how do I organize my ideas for AI," "build my second brain for content," "stop AI slop in my writing," or "create a content system that compounds over time." Applies to writers, founders, and marketers who want AI to repeat their voice rather than invent a new one every session.

name: ai-repeat-not-write
title: Use AI to Repeat, Not to Write or Think
desc: Guides use of AI for writing tasks so output preserves the writer's authentic voice instead of producing generic "AI slop." Trigger when a user asks "should I let AI write this for me," "can AI write my post/email/script," or complains that AI-generated content "doesn't sound like me." Enforces the rule that AI should repurpose the writer's own already-written, approved language and phrasing across formats/platforms, never originate net-new thinking or arguments from scratch.

name: build-ownership-through-association
title: Build Ownership Through Association and Personality Details
desc: Helps creators and writers differentiate in crowded niches by building "ownership" of a topic through volume of association plus personality data points (biographical facts, quirks, backstory) rather than radical originality. Triggers on prompts like "how do I stand out," "how do I own a topic," "there's no moat in my niche," or when someone believes a niche is too saturated to differentiate in. Explains that language, words, and even names are unowned/open-source, and ownership is built by repeatedly linking yourself to a topic until audiences associate it with you.

name: engineer-voice-through-word-choice
title: Engineer Voice Through Word Choice and Sentence Structure
desc: Use when a user says AI-generated or ghostwritten content "doesn't sound like me," asks to "fix my voice," or can't pinpoint why writing feels off. Diagnoses voice mismatch as concrete, tunable variables (pronoun perspective, word choice, sentence structure) rather than a vague stylistic trait. Applies the I-perspective vs. you-perspective test to convert generic "commodity" advice content into personality-driven content, and treats single word/phrase swaps as high-leverage fixes for perceived voice mismatch.

name: pick-a-side-on-commodity-debates
title: Pick a Side on Commodity Debates
desc: Use when drafting content on a popular/commodity topic (e.g., finance, productivity, health advice) that risks sounding generic or AI-slop-like. Identifies the standard opposing arguments ("commodity debates") within a niche and forces the writer to commit to an explicit personal stance before drafting, so AI-generated or human-written content doesn't default to bland, both-sides-ism examples the author doesn't actually believe. Trigger on requests like "write about X topic," "this draft feels generic," "make this sound less like AI," or when a piece covers a well-worn subject without a clear point of view.

name: mine-personal-stories-for-signature-lines
title: Mine Personal Stories for Signature Lines
desc: Extracts and refines a personal hook or story into a reusable "signature line" that can be redeployed across dozens of pieces of content. Trigger when a user says "I don't have anything interesting to write about," "how do I make my story stick," "I keep repeating myself and it feels wrong," or asks how to build a recognizable personal narrative/point of view. Uses a test-observe-repeat loop (e.g., the Quora World of Warcraft example) where a specific phrasing is tested publicly, resonance is measured, and the exact wording is then repeated verbatim across content to build audience association.

name: humanize-brand-content-with-named-personalities
title: Humanize Brand Content With Named Personalities
desc: Use when a brand or company social account reads as flat, corporate, or "AI slop" compared to personal creator accounts. Trigger on phrases like "how do we make our brand content less corporate," "branded content isn't working," or "our company account has no personality." Covers assigning real, named employees (not just the CEO/founder) as recurring on-camera or written personalities behind brand posts, using commodity-brand humanization tactics (e.g., a named employee persona like Taco Bell's "Tiffany") to make company content feel authored by a person rather than a faceless institution.

name: evaluate-timely-vs-timeless-content
title: Evaluate Content on the Timely-vs-Timeless Spectrum
desc: Evaluates whether a piece of content or writing idea is worth creating by classifying it on the timely-vs-timeless spectrum. Trigger when deciding what to write next, whether to chase a trend, whether an idea justifies the effort involved, or when asking "is this worth writing/making" for scripts, newsletters, or short-form video. Helps set correct distribution expectations so timeless work isn't judged by short-term/meme-level metrics.

name: overcome-publishing-fear-set-volume-baseline
title: Overcome Publishing Fear and Set a Volume Baseline
desc: Deploys when a user hesitates to publish content due to self-doubt about their voice, originality, or ideas, or when they ask how much content they should be producing. Triggers on phrases like "I don't like my voice," "this isn't original enough," "am I just repeating what others said," or "how much should I be posting." Addresses the psychological block of comparing one's work to established creators and replaces vague quality anxiety with a concrete volume target as baseline production infrastructure, to be established before optimizing for quality or originality.
